definitions.explanation: A printing method using raised metal or wooden type pieces that are inked and pressed onto paper, or the type pieces themselves.

examples.japanese: この{本|ほん}は{活版|かっぱん}{印刷|いんさつ}で{刷|す}られている。
examples.english: This book was printed using letterpress.

examples.japanese: {活版|かっぱん}{印刷|いんさつ}の{名刺|めいし}は{独特|どくとく}の{風合|ふうあ}いがある。
examples.english: Letterpress-printed business cards have a distinctive texture.

examples.japanese: {活版|かっぱん}{印刷|いんさつ}は{明治時代|めいじじだい}に{日本|にほん}で{広|ひろ}く{普及|ふきゅう}したが、{現在|げんざい}では{趣味|しゅみ}やアートとして{再評価|さいひょうか}されている。
examples.english: Letterpress printing became widespread in Japan during the Meiji era, and today it is being reevaluated as a hobby and art form.

notes:
A compound of {活|かつ} (movable/living) and {版|ぱん} (printing plate/block). The word is short for {活字版|かつじばん} (movable type printing plate). This technology was revolutionary for mass-producing printed text.

Although largely replaced by offset printing and digital methods for commercial use, letterpress has experienced a revival as a craft. Workshops offering {活版|かっぱん}{印刷|いんさつ} experiences are popular in Japan, and many stationery enthusiasts seek out letterpress-printed postcards and business cards for their tactile quality — the slight indentation left by the type on paper.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {活版|かっぱん}{印刷|いんさつ}: letterpress printing
- {活版|かっぱん}{印刷機|いんさつき}: letterpress printing press
- {活版|かっぱん}{印刷所|いんさつじょ}: letterpress printing shop

RELATED TERMS:
- {活字|かつじ}: movable type; printed text
- {版画|はんが}: woodblock print
- {印刷|いんさつ}: printing
